QF.id: AIFM CII Fund Performance and Benchmarking_6

question.text: Kaveri Growth AIF drew INR 100 crore at t=0, paid INR 5 crore of fees and expenses at end of each of Y1 through Y4 (paid out-of-pocket at the fund), and distributed INR 180 crore at end of Y5 (net of all fees/carry/tax). The approximate Net IRR at the investor level is:

explanation.text: **The Logic:** Investor cash flows: -100 at t0, -5 each at t1..t4, +180 at t5. Solve XIRR: sum of PV = 0. Approximating: at 9.5%, PV(-100) + PV(-5@1..4) + PV(180@5) ≈ -100 - 5*(3.204) + 180/1.573 = -100 -16.02 +114.44 ≈ -1.58. At 9.3% it balances. Net IRR ≈ 9.5%. The Cat I/II rule: include all fee/expense outflows at investor-level to get Net IRR. **The Trap:** 7.5% underestimates; 12.5% ignores the intermediate fee drag; 15% is close to Gross IRR of a similar cash profile without the fee outflows. **Cross-Exam Context:** Same mechanics appear in XIX-C and XIX-A (distribution side). XXI-B PMS uses time-weighted returns so intermediate client additions/withdrawals don't distort the manager's track record. **Manager's Pro-Tip:** When pitching re-ups, Cat I/II managers should compute Net IRR with the actual ACTUAL fee-draw calendar (typically quarterly in arrears), not an annual lump-sum. The difference can be 50-80 bps and shows sophistication to institutional LPs.
